validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + DUPLICATE re-audit. The gem.wiki page is a stub: Location and Start Year blank, no endpoints, no route, and its SOLE citation is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' (wiki_citations.json confirms exactly one reference). The OPEC ASB is a country-level statistics compendium and does NOT name individual pipelines, so this row's only support is a generic aggregate that does not name a 'Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha' line. Every web trace of the exact name 'Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha gas pipeline' resolves back to GEM itself; no independent source names this specific 470 km / 42 in / 11.03 bcm/y line. That is a self-referential-support flag. HOWEVER the underlying physical thing is real: independent sources document a 42-inch Iraqi 'national dry gas pipeline' backbone. The Iraqi Economists Network report (Ahmed A. Al-Jibawi, 2025, 'Shedding Light on Recent Oil & Gas Pipeline Projects in Iraq', iraqieconomists.net) repeatedly references 'the 42-inch national dry gas pipeline' as an existing trunk that other lines bifurcate from and feed into (e.g. the Feb-2025 Shatt Al-Basrah 42-inch line joining it; the Gharraf 20-inch line joining 'the 42-inch national dry gas pipeline'; a 42-inch line bifurcating from the national dry gas pipeline at Mahmoodia south of Baghdad). [That PDF is a legitimate independent source but url_verifier cannot read PDF byte streams, so it is cited here in notes rather than in proposed_refs.] Rawabet Center's history of Iraqi gas confirms a 'national network of gas... extends from the south to Baghdad and the center to meet the northern network to Kirkuk', with power stations built at al-Nasiriyah, Hilla and Najaf in the 1980s. So: the 42-inch national dry-gas trunk physically exists and serves the Nasiriyah/central corridor. The problem is that GEM appears to have captured this ONE backbone (plus its feeder branches) as MULTIPLE overlapping rows: P4061 'National Gas Pipeline' (600 km, 42 in) and P1852 'Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha' (470 km, 42 in) are both the 42-inch national dry-gas trunk under two names; and the 'Trans-Iraq(i)' family (P1852 trunk + P4062/P4064/P4065/P4066 short 24/18-in branches to Hilla/Najaf/Dewania/Daura power stations, all also citing OPEC ASB 2012) looks like one harvested table. CLASSIFICATION is fine (dry-gas transmission trunk, correctly Gas, not an oil/NGL line, distinct from the 42-in crude Strategic Pipeline). SPEC caveat: name says 'Nasriyaha' (Nasiriyah, ~180 km from Basra) but LengthKnown=470 km implies the line reaches the Baghdad area, an internal inconsistency; none of 470 km / 42 in / 11.03 bcm/y could be tied to any source that actually names this line, so all specs are unverified against an independent naming source. Not a phantom, but as entered it is a probable duplicate of P4061 with GEM-only, aggregate-cited specs.

routes.end_name: Nasiriyah, Dhi Qar Governorate (city / power-station gas load)

waypoints.name: Diwaniyah, Al-Qadisiyah Governorate (probable continuation toward Hilla/Baghdad implied by 470 km length)

routes.corridor_desc: Iraq's 42-inch national dry-gas trunk runs from the southern gas-gathering/processing area (Rumaila/Basra) north-northwest across Dhi Qar (Nasiriyah) and up the Euphrates corridor through Muthanna (Samawah) and Qadisiyah (Diwaniyah) toward central Iraq, feeding power stations at Nasiriyah, Hilla and Najaf. The row's name terminates the line at Nasiriyah, but the 470 km length is far longer than Basra->Nasiriyah (~180 km) and closer to Basra->Baghdad, so the true corridor very likely extends past Nasiriyah toward Hilla/Baghdad. Bound is LOOSE: endpoints and corridor are inferred from the documented national-trunk geography, not from a source that maps this specific line. Only the Nasiriyah node is a firm named waypoint.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints inferred from the documented Iraqi national dry-gas network (south->Baghdad/center, Nasiriyah power station) per Rawabet Center; no source geolocates this specific named line. Coordinates are real city/field centroids (Nasiriyah 31.05,46.26; Samawah 31.33,45.28; Diwaniyah 31.99,44.92; Basra/Rumaila hub ~30.5,47.5) used as corridor anchors, NOT surveyed pipeline vertices. No coordinate fabricated: where the exact trunk alignment is unknown I bound it loosely to the Euphrates corridor. Length/name discrepancy (Nasiriyah terminus vs 470 km) noted in validity.

summary: P1852 concern=duplicate: real 42-in Iraqi national dry-gas trunk but GEM-only/OPEC-aggregate-sourced and a probable relabel/segment of P4061 'National Gas Pipeline'; route suggested low (Rumaila/Basra->Nasiriyah->Euphrates corridor).
